Gun law fail: Charleston shooter should not have been able to purchase gun.
The law didn't fail here - the FBI failed. If they (and the agencies they liaise with) had done their job properly in the time allotted to them, the law would have worked just fine.

The whole system failed. So what is the point?

It is like gun free zones. If someone is going to kill folks, a gun free zone won't slow them down. It just limits immediate response by others that are present.

In the cases mentioned, the law itself would have performed as intended had the FBI done what it was supposed to do. This is important because it shows that the solution isn't legislative (i.e. more/stricter laws) but procedural (i.e. make sure the FBI is doing its job), and undermines a lot of the language in the piece. The idea that the three-day period is a "loophole" is silly: it's a statutory response time requirement given to a federal agency, just like the response time requirements for things like FOIA requests and a slew of other things. It exists specifically to stop agencies like the FBI from stalling purchases for political reasons, staffing reasons or flat-out laziness (avoiding wait times like those seen for the ATF Form 4) by giving them an explicit deadline - the FBI failing to meet it is no more a "loophole" than someone getting away with a theft because the local chief was too lazy to send an officer over before the statute of limitations ran out.

The problem with all of this is that while the system as a whole did fail, blaming the wrong part of the system for that failure will lead to the system getting worse, not better. Even if you feel the whole thing is misguided or ineffective, my guess is that you'd feel a lot better with a response that lights a fire under the FBI's rear than one that makes the system more time-consuming, burdensome, invasive and obnoxious for the vast majority of people (i.e. law-abiding gun owners) who deal with it.

Although I agree with tighter background checks, what is the point if the people in charge can't accurately enforce them? We need to make sure the agencies in charge of this sort of thing are able to do what we wan't before passing in more laws.

I don't know how you made this, but my method for cooking steak goes as follows. Cast iron, salt, pepper, olive oil, meat. 4-5 minutes on each side to get a good medium-rare. Dig in. A great trick my grandmother told me was to put the skillet into the oven and get it hot, then put it over the range, and drop your meat ASAP.
In general, I made it like that. Salt, pepper, olive oil, seared to a hot pan. I don't have an oven, but thanks for the trick :)

My favorite is the following. Get meat to room temperature. Pan on medium heat. Season the steaks with salt/pepper (both sides). Add 1-2 Tsp of olive oil to the hot pan. Once the pan begins to lightly smoke, put the steaks in. Sear both sides for 1 minute and cook for a total of 7 minutes or so, for medium (depending on thickness). After searing the first side, add crushed whole garlic cloves (1 per steak) and some twigs of fresh thyme. Mix it in good with the steak. Rub that garlic all over. At the end, add some butter and baste the steaks. Let rest for a few minutes before serving. You'll have a nice golden sear and a very tasty steak. :)

Now that some time has past we might swell talk about some of the aspects of Finland we like/dislike, or some key points on the map worth mentioning!

I'll start by talking note of the choke point (donut) by the west point that separates the far west side of the map from the center. It always seems to pose a threat as a useful flanking outlet even if the only point on the map is in the town. It's usefulness is realized when the only point is at the lake. If you find yourself in an awkward position, where you are the only one guarding it from the east side, hide under the archway so artillery is a non factor.

Personally I have not had a huge amount of success on it yet apart from when ground attacking from aircraft as it would appear that most tanks really stick out and are much easier to see than on some other maps in my opinion. I think that I just need to learn the map better.

Although its just a visual effect I love the way the tracks go though the snow it looks incredible.
